transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I feel like I’m constantly bracing myself—my whole body stays tight all day from worrying about my husband and everything I’m juggling. My primary care doctor actually noticed how incredibly tense I was during a routine visit recently and suggested I seek some help. It has just become so overwhelming to manage it all.
Did these worries and tension start after a specific stressful event or change in your life, or have they been going on for a long time without one clear trigger?

Yes, it really started about seven months ago. My husband was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and mild congestive heart failure nine months ago, and taking on his caregiving duties alongside my community commitments triggered this overwhelming worry and tension.
Since this started, have you also had a low mood or loss of interest in things most days, or has it mainly been worry and tension tied to your husband’s illness and caregiving?

I have lost the enjoyment I used to get from my book club and the art center, but it's mainly because I feel so overwhelmed and tense all the time. My mind is constantly worrying about my husband's health and managing everything, which just leaves me too distracted to actually enjoy those things anymore.
Do you feel your worry and tension are mainly tied to your husband's illness and caregiving stress, or have you also been worrying about many different areas of life most days for at least 6 months?

While my husband's health was the trigger, my worry has definitely spread to other areas, like worrying about letting people down at the art center or if we can afford his changing medicines. This constant worrying and physical tension have been happening almost every day for about seven months now.
Did these worries and tension start within a few months of your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, or had you been having similar anxiety before that without a clear trigger?

Yes, they started about seven months ago, which was just a couple of months after my husband was diagnosed and his care routine became a long-term responsibility. I really didn't have this level of constant anxiety or tension before his illness.
Have your worries and tension gradually improved at all as you’ve adjusted to your husband’s illness, or have they stayed about the same or gotten worse over time?

No, they haven't improved at all—they've actually gotten worse and more overwhelming over the last seven months. Ever since his health routine became a long-term thing, the constant worry has just taken over my life. It finally got to the point where it was too much to handle, which is why I realized I needed to seek help.

Have your symptoms been causing problems mainly because of this specific stressor, or do you also have excessive worry that feels hard to control even when you are not thinking about your husband or caregiving?

Yes, the worry feels completely out of my control and spreads to other things, like whether I'm letting people down at the art center or if we'll have enough money for his medicines. Even when I try to relax, read, or go to my book club, these "what-ifs" just barge right in and I can't seem to stop them.
Have you also been having trouble sleeping, feeling restless, getting fatigued easily, or having muscle tension most days because of the worry?

While I can sleep a full night, I still wake up feeling completely wrung out and fatigued, as if I'm constantly moving through molasses. I also feel incredibly restless, like I've had too much coffee with my legs constantly bouncing, and my shoulders and neck are always knotted up from tension, which even causes evening headaches from clenching my jaw.

Have these symptoms been present for only the period after your husband’s illness and caregiving stress began, or have you had similar ongoing anxiety and tension for longer than that even before this event?

These symptoms have only been present for about seven months, starting after my husband's health issues settled into a long-term routine. I never experienced this kind of ongoing, constant anxiety and physical tension before his illness and my caregiving responsibilities began.

Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?
No, I’ve never had sudden, overwhelming spikes of panic like that. My anxiety is more of a constant, lingering worry and physical tension that stays with me all day long.
Over the past seven months, have you been feeling down or hopeless most days, or is the main problem the worry and tension?

The main problem is definitely the constant worry and physical tension, rather than feeling down or hopeless. While the strain has exhausted me and taken the joy out of my activities, the real driving force is the non-stop worrying about my husband and my commitments. It just keeps my body feeling completely tight, braced, and on edge all day long.

Did these symptoms begin within about 3 months of your husband’s diagnosis and caregiving stress, and are they mainly tied to that stressor? Or do they feel out of proportion to the situation and not limited to it?

Yes, they started about seven months ago, which was about two months after his diagnosis, so definitely within that three-month window. However, the worry has spread to other areas like our finances and letting people down at the art center, and it feels completely out of proportion and impossible to control. It feels like every little hiccup is going to snowball into some terrible disaster.
Have you ever had a period of at least 6 months before this where you were worrying excessively about many different things most days, even without a major stressor like your husband’s illness?

No, I don't recall ever having a period of worry like this in the past before my husband's health problems started. I have always been a busy person, but I was always able to handle my day-to-day life without this kind of constant, overwhelming anxiety.

Did your worry and tension start soon after your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, and have they stayed mainly linked to that stressor? Or did they continue for a long time after you had adjusted to the situation?

Yes, they started about seven months ago, shortly after my husband's health issues settled into a long-term routine. I haven't really adjusted to the situation at all; instead, these feelings have been continuous and the stress of managing his care alongside my other commitments has just remained completely overwhelming.
Have your symptoms mostly improved once you adjusted to your husband’s illness, or have they continued for more than 6 months after the stressor started even without much change in the situation?

No, they haven't improved at all and have continued constantly for about seven months now. Ever since my husband's health problems settled into a long-term routine, I've been stuck in this state of worry and tension without any relief.
Have your symptoms lasted longer than 6 months after the stressful situation started, or did they begin to ease once you had more time to adjust?

Yes, they have lasted for about seven months now and haven't eased up at all. They started right around the time my husband's health problems became a long-term routine, and the worry and tension have just been constant ever since.
Have you been feeling this level of excessive worry and tension for most days over the past 6 months or longer, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?

Yes, I’ve been feeling this way almost every single day for about seven months now. Even on quiet days when there are no medical appointments or immediate problems to deal with, my mind still races with "what-ifs" and my body remains incredibly tight and on edge.
Before your husband’s illness began, did you ever have a long period of excessive worry about many different things for 6 months or more, or is this the first time you’ve had symptoms like this?
No, this is definitely the first time I have ever struggled with symptoms like this. Before my husband's illness, I never experienced this level of constant, overwhelming worry in my life.

Have these worries and physical tension been mainly a response to your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, or do they continue even when you’re not dealing with that stressor and feel out of proportion to it?

While my husband's illness definitely triggered this, the worry and physical tension have taken on a life of their own now. Even when I'm away from caregiving, like trying to relax at my book club, I just can't turn it off and my mind constantly drifts to worst-case scenarios. It feels completely out of proportion because I'm also constantly worrying about other things, like our finances and letting people down at the art center.

Since your husband’s illness and caregiving situation began, have your symptoms mostly been tied to that stressor and gradually eased as you adjusted, or have they continued for more than 6 months after the stressor started and felt out of proportion to it?

They definitely haven't eased up; they have been going on continuously for about seven months now. Instead of adjusting to my caregiving role, the constant worrying and physical tension have persisted and feel completely overwhelming and out of proportion.

Have these symptoms caused you significant problems in work, caregiving, or social activities, and do they seem clearly tied to the stress of your husband’s illness rather than a more general ongoing anxiety pattern?

Yes, they have caused significant problems in my life; I've started skipping or leaving my book club and art planning sessions early because I'm too wound up to follow conversations, and I'm falling behind on basic chores like laundry and bills. While it definitely escalated with the stress of managing my husband's health, it has now snowballed into a constant, general pattern where I worry about absolutely everything, including our finances and letting people down.

Did your anxiety and stress start within 3 months of your husband’s illness and caregiving changes, and do they seem mainly tied to that stressor rather than continuing as a broader worry pattern after the situation changed?

Yes, they started about two months after his diagnosis, which is within that three-month window. However, it hasn't stayed tied just to his illness; it has snowballed into a much broader, constant pattern of worrying about things like our finances and letting people down at the art center. It has now been going on continuously like this for about seven months.
Have your symptoms been improving as you’ve had time to adjust to your husband’s illness, or have they stayed persistent and broad even when the caregiving stress is not actively happening?

No, they haven't improved at all and have remained completely persistent for about seven months now. Even when I am not actively caregiving—like when I'm trying to relax and read in the evening or sitting at my book club—my mind still constantly worries and my body stays incredibly tense.
Have your symptoms been steadily improving as you adjusted to your husband’s illness and caregiving role, or have they stayed persistent and widespread even when the stress is not actively happening?

No, they haven't improved at all and have stayed persistent and constant over the last seven months. Even when there isn't an active caregiving task happening—like when I'm trying to relax, read, or attend my book club—I still feel constantly tense, on edge, and unable to stop the 'what-if' thoughts.

Do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, trembling, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?

No, I don't experience those sudden, overwhelming panic attacks or episodes of intense fear that peak quickly with things like a racing heart or shortness of breath. Instead, my anxiety is a constant, steady background tension and worry that stays with me throughout the entire day.
Have your worries and tension mostly improved as you’ve gotten used to your husband’s illness, or have they stayed strong and broad for more than 6 months after the stress started?

No, they haven't improved at all; instead, they have stayed very strong and constant. It has been about seven months now since my husband's health issues became a long-term routine, and the worries and tension haven't eased up.
Before your husband’s illness began, did you ever have a period of excessive worry about many different things for 6 months or more, or is this the first time you’ve had symptoms like this?
This is the first time I have ever experienced this kind of constant, overwhelming worry. I really didn't have any symptoms like this before my husband became ill and I had to manage his care.
Did your symptoms start within 3 months of your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, or did they begin later and seem more like a general anxiety that is not tied to one stressor?

Yes, they did start within that three-month window—about seven months ago, which was two months after his diagnosis. But even though his illness triggered it, the anxiety has since spread to many other areas of my life, like our finances and letting people down at the art center. It now feels like a constant, general worry that isn't just tied to his health.

As your husband’s health situation has become more familiar, have your worries and tension gradually eased, or have they stayed just as strong even when the caregiving stress is not actively happening?

No, they haven't eased up at all; they have remained constantly strong for about seven months now. Even when I am not actively caregiving, such as when I am trying to relax, read, or attend my book club, the worries and physical tension are still right there. I just can't seem to shake them.

Have these worries and physical tension mainly been a response to your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, or have they continued even after you’ve had time to adjust and the stressor is no longer the main issue?

Although they started around the time of my husband's diagnosis, the worries and tension have actually continued and worsened over the last seven months, even after his health routine settled. Instead of adjusting, I find myself constantly on edge, and my worries have expanded to other areas like my community commitments and our finances. It has really become a constant state of mind rather than just a reaction to his care.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with generalized anxiety disorder: excessive, difficult-to-control worry occurring most days for about 7 months, spreading across multiple domains (husband’s health, finances, community commitments), with marked restlessness, fatigue, muscle tension, and significant functional impairment. Although symptoms began after a caregiving stressor, they became pervasive, persistent, and out of proportion rather than remaining a time-limited adjustment reaction. No panic attacks or primary depressive syndrome were confirmed.
